subtitle: Lesson 21 · The No-Cloning Theorem & Quantum Information

steps.label: If you already know the state, copying is trivial
steps.sub: Just prepare a fresh copy from that knowledge

steps.label: What's forbidden is copying a state you don't know
steps.sub: In classical computing, that's just assignment — Ctrl+C

code:
assume U clones basis states:
U(|0>|0>) = |0>|0>,  U(|1>|0>) = |1>|1>

by LINEARITY, applied to |+> = (|0>+|1>)/sqrt2:
U(|+>|0>) = (|00> + |11>) / sqrt(2)   <- an entangled Bell state!

but a correct clone needs:
|+>|+> = (|00>+|01>+|10>+|11>) / 2   <- all four coeffs = 0.5

these are DIFFERENT states -> CONTRADICTION
caption: Linearity forces an entangled state out; a correct clone needs a clean product state. No U can give both.

steps.label: The proof used no mention of noise or hardware
steps.sub: Only that operators must be unitary (linear)

steps.label: Better engineering will never close this gap
steps.sub: It's a theorem about linear operators, not current technology

steps.label: Same category as 'you cannot divide by zero'
steps.sub: Not 'today's hardware can't do this yet'

steps.label: The failed clone produced something real: entanglement
steps.sub: A recurring pattern — impossible duplication often entangles instead

steps.label: Measuring your way around it doesn't work either
steps.sub: Extracting full info via measurement collapses the state (Chapter 3)

steps.label: Version control, caching, backups all assume free copies
steps.sub: None of that intuition transfers to an unknown qubit
